context: On the left is an undirected graph with five vertices and seven edges. On the right is its 5×5 adjacency matrix. The vertices in V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4] correspond in order to row and column indices 0 through 4. Vertex labels and indices differ. The table headers give both, so look up the indices first.
description: An entry M[i, j]=1 means an edge connects vertex V[i] at index i to vertex V[j] at index j. An entry M[i, j]=0 means there is no edge. An undirected edge is equivalent in either direction, so both M[i, j] and M[j, i] contain 1. The matrix is therefore symmetric across the main diagonal. The graph has no self-loops, so every diagonal entry M[i, i] is 0. The seven undirected edges thus account for 14 entries equal to 1.

Colors link three undirected edges to their pairs of symmetric entries. Edge 1–2 (indices 0 and 2) gives M[0, 2]=1 and M[2, 0]=1. Edge 3–2 (indices 1 and 2) gives M[1, 2]=1 and M[2, 1]=1. Edge 5–4 (indices 3 and 4) gives M[3, 4]=1 and M[4, 3]=1. The table below gives the full matrix.

frames.explanation: To check vertices 3 and 4, find their indices, 1 and 4, and read M[1, 4]=0. No edge connects them. Use the indices in the matrix rather than the vertex labels.

summary: The vertex list determines the row and column indices. The entry at their intersection shows whether an edge connects the two vertices.
